AA Prototype · Requirements catch-up

The catch-up: from the RFP to the catalogue

The prototype was built in July against the original RFP, in fourteen phases. The requirements catalogue has since become the source of truth and moved a long way: Bookings instead of Cards, Slots and Draft Lists, one Contract per Procedure locked at authorise, admin-decided hospital matching, an internal ledger with Xero as its mirror. This plan closes every verified gap in 45 further phases, numbered 14 to 44, each one focused session (at most two) with one coherent deliverable, and every automatic or external event given a demo button on the screen where it matters.

What changed since the prototype

The prototype is the July RFP model with Phases 15 to 32 layered on. Calendar, Slots, Lists, Draft Lists, pairings, tiers, warnings engine, the AA fee run and the Xero simulation are close to the catalogue. Money and intake are not. Of roughly 235 graded items, about 40 Match, about 25 are Partial, about 15 are Missing, and the rest are Contradicts or Grouping. Contradicts dominates EP-02 to EP-08, EP-11 and EP-12: the prototype implements a different, superseded design there, not a smaller version of the new one. EP-01, EP-10 and most of EP-13 are near done. The core is one coordinated rework: Contract (holder, dated versions, lines, flags) replaces billing route plus Type 1/2/3. Pricing, completion, prepayment, invoicing, payer, review and events all hang off it. Statuses were not used to scope work; they appear below only where an open question (OQ) makes a gap unsafe.

The themes below are the gap analysis's own grouping. Each lists the phases that carry its items. Full reasoning: GAP-ANALYSIS.md.

  1. Contract-centred billing model

    Billing route, Type 1/2/3 and protected default Type 1s replaced by holders, dated Contract versions, standalone lines, one No contract (RVG), mandatory Contract per Procedure, staged review, authorisation snapshot. XL, split into model, versioning screens, picker.

    25 items · built in phases 18, 19a, 20, 21, 25

  2. Pricing, units and modifiers

    Price, rate and discount held on the Procedure with no reason, Contract flag gating anaesthetist, no-charge invoice, modifier split above four, RVG hidden-key master, modifier records with explanations, age pre-applied, out-of-range warns, completion rules reworked. XL.

    38 items · built in phases 19, 19a, 19b, 20, 21, 23, 24, 39b

  3. Hospital intake matching screen

    No review-and-merge screen exists; HL7/FHIR and PDF rows auto-apply. Need staged rows, match/create/Draft List/reject, per-row change type, differences for approval, unmatched queue, day move as cancel plus new, edits until AUTHORISED. XL.

    15 items · built in phases 33, 34, 35

  4. NHI mandatory and text as received

    Remove provisional patients and NHI pending; waiting-for-NHI queue; procedure text kept per source with time; separate invoice description. M, bundled with intake.

    10 items · built in phases 20a, 40

  5. Prepayment and holding account

    Prepaid Contract triggers prepayment at line price, admin approval with letter, payable to holding account, second pair at authorise, refund on cancel, no automatic balance. Anaesthetist currently paid before the procedure. XL.

    24 items · built in phases 16, 27, 27a, 36, 41

  6. Events, additional invoices and credit notes

    Post-op addendum Booking replaced by events on the Procedure, free-form additional invoices, credit then rebill, negative payables netted in a weekly payment cycle. XL.

    17 items · built in phases 38b, 39, 39a, 39b

  7. Edit window until AUTHORISED and anaesthetist views

    Anaesthetist edits stay open on SUBMITTED, List leaves main view at AUTHORISED, balances show invoices immediately, search and scroll-back. M.

    11 items · built in phases 31, 38a

  8. OQ-81 reversal: unavailability is never a conflict

    Remove availability conflict kind, make closed sessions non-assignable by the office, route sickness through return-or-assign to a Draft List. M to L, independent.

    7 items · built in phases 30, 31, 32, 32b

  9. Single-Booking move and notification pool

    Anaesthetist moves one Booking into a new List in a colleague's free Slot; pool notices gain resolve tick, count, show-resolved and an ask-the-office source. M.

    12 items · built in phases 28, 32, 32a, 32b

  10. Payer, insurer, balances and warnings

    Payer name and email on the Booking, insurer and approval number on the Booking, patient balance alerts, remaining warning rules, ledger positions, split as a Booking action. L, after Contract rework.

    20 items · built in phases 15a, 21, 22, 36, 40, 42

  11. Profile, reporting and admin polish

    Drop GST period, add bank details, monthly GST of payments passed on, flat owed list, preferred pairing ordering, audit exclusions, cutover load, master calendar, simulated sign-in, scale and privacy demos, point-of-need help. M, mostly small.

    24 items · built in phases 17, 18, 20a, 25, 26, 35, 38, 39, 42, 43, 43a

How this works

  1. Get the owner decisions first. D1 to D11 (the table at the top of ROADMAP.md) each gate one phase. A phase whose answer has not come in builds the stated default and labels it provisional.
  2. Pick the next phase from the table below, respecting the order in "Sequencing and rules". The Contracts track (17 to 25) and the Schedule track (28 to 32) each run strictly in order.
  3. Open a fresh Claude Code session and paste that phase's kick-off prompt. The agent reads the roadmap, its phase doc, the gap detail for its items, the prototype maps and PROGRESS.md before touching anything.
  4. Drift check first. The catalogue keeps moving. Each session diffs its items against d4db277, reports what changed, and adapts the plan before building.
  5. The agent plans and builds straight on. It turns the phase doc into work-sized steps and starts building without waiting for approval, so phases can run back to back (ROADMAP.md "Owner review: agents test themselves").
  6. Every phase ends the same way: npm run build, npm run build:pwa, npx vitest run and (for UI work) npm run shots green; the checklist run and reported item by item; the adversarial review-and-fix pass (PROGRESS convention 18); the demo guide patched for any beat it broke; the catalogue screenshots brought in step with the app (the phase's capture recipes created or updated, then a full npm run capture in requirements-board/ with no failed recipe and npm run verify:board green, PROGRESS convention 19); a PROGRESS.md entry. Agents never commit.
  7. When the catalogue changes, follow README.md: re-grade the changed items, merge them into gaps.json, update the affected phase docs, and re-render this page with node docs/prototype-build/catch-up/tools/build-index.mjs.

Demo buttons live on their screens. Anything that cannot be shown through normal use (scheduled jobs, backend events, external systems) gets a trigger in the harness bar's "Demo actions" menu, listed only on the screen where it matters. The installed PWA has no harness bar, so it gets the same list as a badged demo-actions sheet, plus office stand-ins for beats that wait on the office. Phase 14 builds the mechanism; every later phase registers into it.

The checklists are the contract. Each phase ends with a short manual test checklist. The agent runs it itself in the running app and reports each item with evidence; nothing is handed to the owner per phase. Each PROGRESS entry ends with a "For the owner's review" list, and Phase 44 gathers them into one list for a single review once every catch-up phase is done.

Sequencing and rules

Owner decisions (table at the top of ROADMAP.md), re-read at the 2026-10-20 update (catalogue d4db277). Answered and built as answered: D1 monthly AA fee (16, built); D5 no prepayment gate (15a, 27); D7 own List moves with no confirmation (32, 32a); D8 flat outstanding list (38); D9 a List leaves the anaesthetist's main view at AUTHORISED, found by search (38a); D10 and D22 free-form additional invoices and credit notes to any party (38b, 39); D11 the NHI mandatory, no-NHI intake rows wait (33, 40); D13 events, now including billing events (38b, 39b); D14 and D15 Slots and the notification pool (built); D18 the Split button (22); D19 on-demand update email, manual (35); D21 a negative with no later payment handled outside (39a); D23 prepayment only for a person paying (27); D24 the balance threshold from the invoice date (40); D26 the RVG multi-procedure rule with no switch (23); D27 no longer arises (27); D32 Contracts may hold no lines (18, 19a, 20); D33 no procedure to match, the RVG code optional (20, 21, 33); D38 the prepayment pair at admin approval, payable to the prepay holding account, a second pair at authorisation, no repoint (27, 27a); D39 the RVG groups are the one master list (19); D40 no time band, the editable flag per Contract (19a, 24); D41 a split before sending is a normal admin edit (39); D42 the office keeps anaesthetists' price lists (19a); D43 P1 included, pre-applied and removable (19b); D44 preferences admin-only (built); D45 versions never backdated (18, 25); D46 no Draft List browsing (built); D50 the per-Contract editable flag and the office changing any price with no reason (18, 24); D58 notices active or resolved and alert the office (32b); D59 unavailability never a conflict (32b); D60 the vacated-session choice for everyone (32b); D61 a single Booking only to a free colleague as a new List (32a); D62 a day move is cancel plus new (33); D63 edits until AUTHORISED (38a, 20); D64 prepaid is a Contract setting (18, 26, 27). Superseded readings, struck in the table: D2, D3, D6, D12, D16, D17, D20, D37. Open, built as their defaults and labelled provisional: D28 (part), D29 to D31, D34 to D37, D47 to D49, D51 to D57. Built: 14 to 17 and 28 to 32; their docs are frozen and their covers keep what they delivered; follow-up work goes to 32a, 32b, 38a, 26, 27, 27a, 39 and 43a. RV ids were renumbered by the 2026-10-20 reverse check: the old RV ids on built 15, 15b, 16, 28 and 32 left their covers and every RV unit was placed by meaning; DM ids are stable. Run order from here: 32a, 32b, 38a, then 18, 19, 19a, 19b, 20 to 25 strictly in order, 26 (needs nothing unbuilt; before 38), 27 then 27a back to back, then Intake (33 after 20a and 31; 34 after 33; 35 after 17, 25, 32, 33) and Money (36 after 16, 22, 25, 27a; 37 and 38 after 36; 38b after 36 and 38a; 39 after 38b; 39a after 37 and 39), 39b after 24, 38a and 38b, 40 after 15a, 34, 36 and 39, 40a after 26 and 40, 41 after 27a, 32a and 39, 42 after 17, 18, 19, 19a, 19b, 25, 29 and 30, 43 after 34, 36, 37 and 42, 43a after 20a, 21, 24, 31 and 39b, 44 last. 38a runs before the Contracts track because a List now leaves the main view at AUTHORISED (no billing dependency) and 20's Contract change needs its edit window. Contracts track: 18 rebuilds holders and Contracts with settings and dated versions, keeping today's terms and route; 19 the RVG groups and type-ahead; 19a standalone lines, starting values, combinations and price lists; 19b modifiers; 20 needs 38a and leaves interims (who is billed via the holder else the existing override else the patient until 21; funderOverride until 22; prepayment read from the Contract's prepaid setting with prepaymentDetail until 27); 20 owns removing PatientPaymentCategory everywhere, 27 removes only the deposit and split paths and prepaymentDetail; 20a straight after 20; 24 values on the Procedure and the editable flag; 25 staged changes and the lock. 24 removes only the rate x time line; 39b removes BillingLine once billing events exist. The pricing model (AR-29 and AR-30, v6 overwritten in place, the v4 regions gone; AR-28 the v6 executive summary) is Greg's proposal: field names for orientation, the catalogue wins (no price step order, modifiers as our records); every pricing phase keeps it in one place in aa-prototype/src/domain/billing behind types the UI reads. BCTI granularity stays one per receivable invoice, counted only by 16's function, labelled provisional; prepayment pairs stay out of the count unless its switch says otherwise. Old-model matches (FT-03.2, US-05.2.1, US-05.2.7, US-05.3.5, US-08.2.1, FT-05.5) are carried across with parity tests. Vocabulary: Booking; move or reassign; no 'slot' in app copy; List states DRAFT (Draft List), ACTIVE, SUBMITTED, AUTHORISED; Not preferred and Preferred; no procedure list, 'RVG code' for the pick; the rooms', the hospital's and the invoice descriptions kept apart; no first or third party; start and finish, never handover; 'event' in one label; the prepaid amount never an estimate or deposit, held in the prepay holding account; notices active or resolved; 'alert the office'. Every phase opens with a drift check against d4db277 and closes green (build, build:pwa, vitest, shots where UI changes, review pass, recipes and capture with verify:board, PERSIST_VERSION when the seed changes, Decisions log updated for superseded rulings, a PROGRESS entry with its owner-review list).

Billing After phase 21 1 session plan doc ↗ 9 items covered

Every invoice is issued in the anaesthetist's name with AA as agent, and is laid out and delivered as its Contract says. The ACCPAY carries provisional buyer-created wording, one per receivable invoice.

Primary Procedure and the multi-procedure rule

Contracts After phases 19b, 22 2 sessions plan doc ↗ 6 items covered

Give every Booking exactly one primary Procedure, shown first, that anyone with edit rights can change through 'Make primary' on mobile, web, Admin and the inbound feed. Calculated Procedures are priced as a whole Booking under the RVG default multi-procedure rule, the one system-wide rule (D26, OQ-90 answered 2026-10-19), with no switch and no provisional label. Base units sit on the primary only. Time units go on every Procedure from its own start and finish times. Modifier units stay on the primary while the total is four or fewer, otherwise they split as evenly as possible with the remainder to the primary (7 over 3 is 3, 2, 2). A fixed-price Procedure keeps its price. Which Procedure is primary is still unsettled, so the first stays primary until someone changes it. The logic lives in one pure module in aa-prototype/src/domain/billing with worked examples. Combinations are no longer in this phase (19a owns them).

- The office's manual fix never edits a master: supplyLockedReference fills a blank, declared holder reference on a failed case (no pricing field), and relockHeldBackBooking sets a Contract valid on the date and re-locks only a held-back Booking that has no invoice. While working:

- Mock backend only. Every new write (assign, move, Slot status, Slot times, default times, horizon, start date, active, cover marker) is a store action through the audited mutate(), with before/after metas and timestamps from the demo clock. Components never own domain state.
- No "slot" in app copy (OQ-64). The UI, the audit labels, the field labels and every new message say session, AM or PM; "Slot" stays a code and planning word (types, ids, file names, this plan). Add the check in work item 22 that greps the touched screens for it.
- One mechanism (OQ-17, OQ-27, OQ-64, answered). Availability is a status held on the Slot (free by default, unavailable, holiday), written directly by setAvailability; there is no availability master and nothing is reconciled. Phase 29's calendar will edit the same field and turn the values into a user-maintained list, so every label goes through the one lookup, displayStatusLabel.
- One derivation. The displayed status comes only from the pure displayStatusKey(slot, list) in src/domain/slots.ts: the List's kind when a List is in the Slot (the List shows in place of the status), the Slot's status otherwise. It takes no Bookings. Delete displayStatusKeyForList and every other derivation from cards, hospital or surgeon. Mobile, web, admin and every finder (US-01.4.2) read the same Slot views and the same isOpenSlot, so a session looks the same everywhere and a session holding a List is never offered as free.
- Keep the six-colour design language: DisplayStatusKey is the same six keys, the Slot statuses plus the List kinds are exactly those six, and the theme parity test still holds. List kind (private, public, pre-op) is a List attribute the catalogue does not model: keep it and list it for the owner.
- Generation follows US-01.1.1 (Confirmed) and OQ-81 part 1: only active anaesthetists, from their start date; every new Slot written free; then the anaesthetist's calendar; then recurring bookings. The RNG fill goes on every generated date (rolled days, new anaesthetists, horizon extensions), weekends included. Recurring bookings keep today's weekday-only guard (Phase 30 adds weekend patterns). A recurring booking that meets an unavailable Slot is traced as a clash, not projected (Phase 31 makes it a Draft List).
- The horizon is a setting (FT-01.1): appSettings.schedule.horizonMonths, 4 by default, beside the default AM and PM times, in one schedule-settings record. Every horizon reader goes through horizonFor(today, months). Extending generates the new days; shortening drops far-edge Slots and empty Lists and refuses while a List there holds Bookings.
- Determinism first. Before touching the generator, commit a golden fixture of today's canvas (the demo window 2026-07-07 to 2026-08-16 and the far edge) and seeded Bookings. The seed keeps today's slot-RNG content inside that fixed window as recorded history (seedRecordedWindow, same per-slot draws), so the window and every Booking reproduce exactly; the far-edge section is regenerated once, deliberately, when the RNG fill goes. Projected Lists keep their L-<reg>-<date>-<session> ids (never parsed to find a Slot); runtime Lists take LG####; Slots are S-<reg>-<date>-<session>. Bump PERSIST_VERSION by one and extend the migrate test.
- Start date and active (US-01.1.3, FT-01.1). Anaesthetist gains a required startDateISO; seeded anaesthetists start before the horizon, so the golden fixture holds. No Slot exists before a start date, or from today for an inactive anaesthetist, on any path (seed, Add, Edit, roll-forward, horizon extension). Add generates from the later of the start date and the demo clock's today; editing the date or the active flag adds or removes Slots from today on and refuses when a removed Slot holds a List.
- The Admin Day grid's roster comes from rosterForDate (the anaesthetist master, every anaesthetist with a Slot that day), not the static cast array, so added anaesthetists appear (US-01.4.2). The Day view's date picker is bounded by the horizon, with a "Beyond the schedule horizon" state.
- Delete listForSlot rather than re-implementing it, so the compiler shows every caller (including the Phase 14 registry entries stage-post-op and ingest-pdf-row). Each caller must handle "no List in this Slot": integrations park instead of silently retiming, the post-op addendum creates its List in today's open session (interim until 38b), the PDF picker and the Move Booking picker offer Lists only.
- Session 1 must end green and demoable: the drawer, phone advice, Edit list, Reassign and Add anaesthetist get the minimal re-point the compiler forces (work item 12, "compile-forced minimums"), and session 2 finishes them. Roll-forward and addAnaesthetist read the seed's SEED_LEAVE once masters.availability is gone.
- Assignment needs a surgeon and a hospital and is an office action (US-01.3.3); a closed hospital is flagged on the new List, never blocked. Assigning onto an unavailable or holiday session is refused for now and labelled interim (Phase 30 makes it accept-and-flag). The surgeon picker is 17's SurgeonPicker (not-preferred surgeons in their own group), a not-preferred choice shows 17's NotPreferredWarning with "Assign anyway", and assignListToSlot writes 17's list.pairingAcknowledged for an office actor through notPreferredEntryIds: warn, never block (US-01.3.5, OQ-43). Phone advice now assigns first, so its acknowledgement moves from onBookingCreated to the assignment, written once. Add store/slotActions.ts to officePrivacy.test.ts's allowlist.
- A Slot holding a List that the anaesthetist marks unavailable keeps its List with a conflict flag, labelled interim: Phase 32 builds return to the office or assign to a colleague (US-01.5.5).
- Reassign moves the List between Slots: same id, Bookings and history; target session open; the vacated session returns to Free by default (OQ-84's recommendation, provisional in the Decisions log), with Unavailable or Holiday on request. No absorb, no regenerate. Candidates are open sessions (isOpenSlot) still shown through 17's AnaesthetistCandidates (groups, tier order, shuffle, filter, Preferred pills). Keep 17's acknowledgement for an office move onto a not-preferred pairing, in reassignList (the office entry point), not in moveListToSlot, which Phases 32 and 32a reuse for the anaesthetist's own moves and which must read, check and log no preference (US-01.4.5). A move recalculates no prepayment and no invoice (US-06.3.5, US-06.5.4: an honour system); if any re-check sits on reassignList or reassignBooking, remove it with its tests and log it. Mark moveListToSlot as the seam for Phase 41's payee repoint (OQ-80) and build nothing for it.
- The office availability finder (work item 20; US-01.4.2, US-01.3.5, US-01.3.6): "Find available" in the Admin Day header opens a sheet listing everyone with an open session that day and session, through 17's rankAnaesthetistCandidates and AnaesthetistCandidates only (tier order, shuffled within a tier from a date, session and suggestionSeq key, the tier filter, and with a surgeon chosen the not-preferred group apart); picking a row opens Assign List with that surgeon. Admin only: the mobile and web finders stay name-ordered with no tier or preference, and 17's privacy test stays green.
- Default AM and PM times live in the schedule-settings record; per-Slot overrides live on the Slot and travel with a reassigned List. Remove the four hardcoded duplicates. A session keeps its default shape on the grid even with one Booking (US-01.1.4's note).
- Empty Slots carry no List state. Every List created by assignment or projection is ACTIVE (15b's rename); print states as 15b does (ACTIVE, SUBMITTED, AUTHORISED), with no "Open" label; DRAFT and "Draft List" stay free for Phase 31.
- Use the catalogue's words in new copy: "reassign" or "move", not "swap"; "recurring booking" where the catalogue says it (the Permanent List screens are renamed in Phase 30, not here).
- Stay in scope: no Draft Lists, pairing enforcement, availability calendar or status editor, conflict clearing or colour change, return-or-assign, anaesthetist move flow or update email.
- One demo trigger: the PWA-only, badged office stand-in "Office assigns a List to my next free session" on Mobile Lists, with its body in src/store/officeStandIn.ts (acting as OFFICE_SIMULATION_ACTOR, "today" from the demo clock, scanning to the horizon end) and its entry in the shared registry; its three fixed choices are pinned by a seed test as never a not-preferred pairing with Dr Souter, and its body reads no preference (it is in the PWA closure). Nothing is added to the harness bar or the Control Panel page, because every office action in this phase, the horizon change included, is demoable through the Admin app in the framed build.
- Design: teal the only action colour, crimson unused on the new sheets, Admin sheets through useSurface().Overlay, and no en or em dashes in any app copy.
- Keep npm run build, npm run build:pwa and npx vitest run green as you go. Add Vitest tests for the Slot module, the generator (order, free by default, active only, clashes), the store actions (refusals, audit, identity, one mechanism, independence from Bookings, horizon, start date, active, roster, three-app and finder parity) and the seed invariants.

Phase goal: the canvas becomes Slots and Lists. Every active anaesthetist has an AM and a PM Slot per day from their start date to the end of a configurable horizon (four months), written free and then painted with their calendar and the surgeons' recurring bookings, with no invented sessions; the status on the Slot is the one mechanism, with no record reconciled into Lists. A List is created only when the office assigns one (or a recurring booking projects it) and then shows in place of the status. The displayed status never depends on Bookings and matches in all three apps and the finders, added anaesthetists appear on the Admin Day grid, default times and the horizon come from one setting, Reassign moves a List between Slots intact with no prepayment re-check, the office's finder lists the available anaesthetists by priority tier with not-preferred pairings apart through Phase 17's helper (never in the anaesthetist apps), every new List is ACTIVE, and the UI never says "slot".

Demo triggers and risks

No new demo triggers: this phase demos through normal use.

Risks. Final status values are to be defined with AA's users: seed the owner's starting set and keep it data. The design's six colours include private, public and pre-op, which the catalogue has no List kind for: keep them as the List's own display, not Slot statuses, and log it for the owner's review. Series need a recurrence rule with per-instance exceptions on the demo clock, kept pure and tested. The theme must read status records instead of a hardcoded union (the statusKeyParity test goes) without breaking the design language. Keep List states out of the status master. The web app stays desktop-width. No 'slot' in app copy. Catalogue screenshots: US-01.2.2's shot shows the editable status master with no List states in it.

While working:
- Invoke the /frontend-design:frontend-design skill before building or reshaping any UI (screens, sheets, dialogs, panels, rows, banners, pills, empty and error states), and apply it inside this repo's design system: the docs/design files and src/theme tokens stay authoritative (convention 17, ROADMAP.md "Front-end design"), so use the skill for layout, hierarchy, spacing, states and finish, never for a new palette, typeface or visual language. Store, seed and pure-domain steps do not need it.
- Mock backend only. Every write goes through a store action and the audited mutate(), with before/after metas and demo-clock timestamps. Components never own domain state. setAvailabilityRange, clearAvailability, createAvailabilitySeries and deleteAvailabilitySeries are each one mutate(), all or nothing on refusal, with one audit entry plus one entry per List affected.
- One mechanism (OQ-27 and OQ-64 answered): the calendar writes the Slot's own status directly. A series is a rule (weekdays, sessions, every 1 to 4 weeks, start, optional until) plus exceptions; it writes its Slots, and a single-instance edit or delete is stored as an exception so no later series write, clock roll forward or horizon extend overwrites it. Nothing reads availability from anywhere but Slots. A series fills only Slots at the default status and in no other series, and reports the rest as left as they are. One helper, seriesCalendarFor, feeds active series (with their exceptions) into 28's generateCanvasForDates as calendar input on every generating path (rollCanvasForward, setHorizonMonths when extending, an earlier start date or a reactivation), so they are painted with the anaesthetist's calendar BEFORE recurring bookings (OQ-81 part 1, settled). A recurring booking on a series-closed session is then never placed: 28's generator returns it as a RecurringClash, which Phase 31 turns into a Draft List. The generator's closed test reads isClosed over the status records; it still draws no RNG. Series rules live in src/domain/availabilitySeries.ts, pure and tested.
- The Slot status set becomes a user-maintained master list (masters.slotStatuses, US-01.2.2), availability values only. Each status has a fixed internal ID (SlotStatusKey) that rules read, never its label; seeded IDs are 28's stored values (free, holiday, unavailable), and an added status gets a generated ST#### ID, shown read only and never edited. Label, long label, description, colour (one of the six design tokens) and treatment are editable, plus "open for bookings" and "anaesthetists can set". Seed the owner's starting set: Free (default, dashed), Holiday (long label "On holiday") and Unavailable (hatched), with today's colours. No "available for emergency" and no extra kinds of unavailable seeded; an admin can add them (Greg: several kinds of unavailable, same effect). A rename or recolour shows in every view with every rule unchanged, and an added status works with no code change (US-01.2.2's two criteria; test both). No provisional line anywhere.
- The List types (private, public, pre-op) stay a fixed List attribute with their own tokens, so a session holding a List shows the List in its place with the design's List colours; no status ID can equal a List kind. Log on the "For the owner's review" list that the catalogue has no List kind.
- Availability is not the List's state (US-01.2.2 since 2026-10-07): the status master, the display key, the legends and the filters never hold DRAFT, ACTIVE, SUBMITTED or AUTHORISED. ListState and its chip stay on the List, untouched. validateSlotStatusDraft refuses a label or long label that is a List state or its label (plus "Draft" and "Draft List", ready for Phase 31), the Availability statuses header says this is a session's availability, not a List's state (Draft, Active, Submitted, Authorised), and the table marks rows "In use" or "Retired", never "Active". Log the guard on the "For the owner's review" list.
- The only closed sets left are the palette (the six Design Language status tokens in src/theme/statusColours.ts, same hexes) and the List types. No new hex anywhere. The hatched and dashed treatments generalise with tokens only, and today's exact strings must still come out for the seeded statuses and every List.
- No literal availability keys outside src/domain/slotStatus.ts and the seed. Finders, filters, counts and clashes use isOpenForBooking, isClosed and isOpenSlot. Only what counts as free changes: the office finder's priority-tier ordering, its not-preferred group and Phase 17's soft not-preferred warning (wired in by 28) stay as they are, and the anaesthetists' own finders stay untiered.
- Availability is never merged into the List. A List in a Slot shows in place of the status. The clash comes from one pure function, availabilityClash: a bookable status clears that List's availability conflict and raises nothing; a closed status over a List flags it once, replacing rather than stacking, with the List's surgeon, hospital, Bookings, times and List type untouched. That flag is the interim for one settled rule, Phase 32's return-or-assign (US-01.5.5) when an anaesthetist marks a session holding a List unavailable; its doc comment says so, and says generation never reaches it (a recurring booking on a closed session is traced as 28's clash for Phase 31's Draft List, not placed and flagged). Do not build the return-or-assign prompt here.
- Honest copy: remove the false "a conflict was flagged and the office notified" line and the false-conflict message with the Free and Block buttons. No line anywhere says the office was notified or told; the interim says the List is flagged on the office's Day view.
- Vocabulary (OQ-64): "slot" never reaches app copy, including labels, result lines, refusals, validator messages and audit labels. Say session, AM or PM, day off and availability. The Admin master is "Availability statuses" (view param availability-statuses). Slot stays a code name. The status validator also refuses "slot" in admin-entered labels.
- One display key space: the display key is list.kind when a List is in the Slot, otherwise slot.status unchanged, typed ListKind | SlotStatusKey. Rename 28's SlotStatus union to SlotStatusKey = string first (so the compiler lists every reader), then reuse the name SlotStatus for the master record; 28's DisplayStatusKey union goes.
- 28's store refusals read the helpers: assignListToSlot (slotNotAvailable) and moveListToSlot (targetNotOpen) refuse isClosed Slots, invalidKind checks LIST_KINDS, requestCover's notFree reads isOpenSlot, and reassign's vacatedStatus defaults to defaultSlotStatus, with the vacated-session picker listing the active statuses (what it should offer is OQ-84, Phase 32's). 28's setAvailability keeps its signature, outcome and slot.status audit, and shares the range action's per-Slot write and clash rule.

- List states: an assigned List is ACTIVE (15b), a DRAFT List is a Draft List (Phase 31). The projection creates ACTIVE Lists, updates and removes only its own empty ACTIVE Lists, and never touches a DRAFT, SUBMITTED or AUTHORISED List. Never label an assigned List "DRAFT" in copy.
- A conflict is only what the catalogue keeps at 60e2d1e (unchanged since 3d3a18c): a List at a closed hospital, or a List (and its Bookings) in a session already marked unavailable. A recurring booking landing on an unavailable session is not a conflict: the projection and generator skip it and report it as skipped, and Phase 31 turns it into a Draft List. An anaesthetist marking a booked session unavailable is return-or-assign (US-01.5.5, Phase 32): build no prompt and no Draft List conversion here; until 32 it is flagged as a named interim, through 29's per-Slot write helper, the one place 32 hooks in. A sickness the office records (the anaesthetist phones in) keeps the List and its Bookings and is a conflict: that is the one provisional reading (OQ-81 part 3), kept on the trigger and the seed and on the "For the owner's review" list.
- Never put the word "slot" in app copy (OQ-64): say session, AM or PM. Slot stays a code word. Status words come from Phase 29's status master labels; rules key on the fixed status ID.
- A conflict clears when its clash goes (holiday deleted or moved, hospital changed, Slot marked available, List reassigned to an available anaesthetist) or when the office clears it. An office clear holds only while its cause stands, needs no reason, and can be undone with "Flag again".

- The DRAFT state. ListState becomes 'DRAFT' | 'ACTIVE' | 'SUBMITTED' | 'AUTHORISED', and List is a union on it: AssignedList (ACTIVE, SUBMITTED or AUTHORISED, with an anaesthetist and a Slot) and DraftList (DRAFT, no anaesthetist, no Slot, a draft trail). LIST_STATE_LABELS gains DRAFT, shown only on a Draft List beside "Unassigned"; no assigned List reads "DRAFT" or "Open". Only an ACTIVE List can be completed and submitted; submitting or authorising a Draft List refuses with "Assign an anaesthetist first.". A store-wide invariant test holds FT-07.1: every ACTIVE, SUBMITTED or AUTHORISED List has its anaesthetist, Slot, day, session, hospital and surgeon, and every DRAFT List has neither anaesthetist nor Slot.
- A Draft List is a List record, plus a draft trail (origin, source, since, by, and for a recurring clash the day it stands for). There is no separate collection, so its Bookings hang off its List id and assignment keeps the id.
  - createDraftList and the recurring clash write through one insertDraftList and leave schedule.slots and every other List untouched; prove it with a test.
  - Only assignDraftList takes DRAFT to ACTIVE, through attachListToSlot, in the session its day and session fix (the admin chooses only the anaesthetist), in one commit with a draftList.assign meta (before state DRAFT, after ACTIVE); the draft trail is kept with assignedAtISO. 15a's warnings are derived on read (store/warnings.ts), so they need no call, but their rules and OpenWarningRow must tolerate a Booking on a Draft List.
  - An ACTIVE List only becomes a Draft List through detachListToDraft, built and unit-tested here for Phase 32 (origins movedToOffice and unavailableReturn); it refuses a SUBMITTED or AUTHORISED List, and no screen in this phase calls it.
  - removeDraftList soft-removes and refuses while it holds an active Booking; redateDraftList moves it and its Bookings to another day and keeps its waiting time.
  - A Draft List cannot be submitted, authorised or billed, and an anaesthetist cannot add a Booking to one.
  - No projection, roll forward or new-anaesthetist path may overwrite a List id a Draft List holds, and a recurring booking never projects a second List or Draft List for a day it already answered for (the Draft List keeps recurringBookingId, and a recurring clash keeps the day in draft.projectedFor even after a re-date or a removal).
- Prepayment (US-06.3.5, US-06.5.4, D20). A Booking on a Draft List has no anaesthetist, so 27's routine generates and withdraws nothing for it. Phase goal: a List with no anaesthetist is a Draft List, the first state (DRAFT) of a List's lifecycle. Each has a hospital, surgeon, day and session, all required, may already hold Bookings, and takes no Slot. Draft Lists are flagged "Unassigned" with their waiting time and sorted soonest first, beside the day in the right rail, in a band on the Day dashboard, on their own Admin page and on a nav badge. Only the office assigns one, by choosing the anaesthetist from everyone potentially available, grouped and tier-ordered by Phase 17's helper with soft warnings and a full audit, and it becomes ACTIVE; or the office removes it or changes its date. A recurring booking that lands on a session the anaesthetist has already marked unavailable becomes a Draft List. Every List has exactly one hospital and one surgeon, and the Day dashboard shows each block's booking count.

Explicit save and the update email

Intake After phases 17, 25, 32, 33 2 sessions plan doc ↗ 7 items covered

Admin Booking editing becomes draft-then-save: Save, Discard and an unsaved-changes warning (US-02.3.2, RV-28). Each save writes one change set, shown as grouped history with an as-at view. The office edits every field until the List is AUTHORISED: the NHI (mandatory, never cleared), the RVG code, the Contract and the invoice description. It can add a Booking to a booked List with a hand-entered Procedure description kept as source text, and never edits the received text. Every Admin Booking has an on-demand, manual-only mailto "Draft update email". The admin picks changes from the history and starts from a per-kind template. It goes to the rooms for a Booking change and the hospital for a cover change, also from a List-move notice and optionally from a single-Booking move. Anaesthetist flows keep immediate saves, and their edits until AUTHORISED land in the same history.

The admin picks one or more rows from the history (saves, creations, cancellations, moves, applied hospital rows, coalesced anaesthetist edits, cover changes); only those appear, netted per field. It starts from the admin-maintained template for the kind of change (Change of anaesthetist, Cancellation, Correction of an error, Booking change), editable in Master data. Opening the mail client writes one "Update email drafted (not sent)" entry and nothing else; nothing is stored or labelled as sent. The whole encoded link is at most 2,000 characters (one labelled constant), and a shortened body says so. Only the allowlisted fields appear (a Procedure named by its RVG group's description, else "Procedure 2"): never an NHI, date of birth, internal notes, the text as received, the invoice description, the RVG code, Contract or holder, payer or insurance indication, modifiers and explanations, money, or pairing preferences and tiers (17's office-private slice), and a List email names no patient. Money After phases 16, 22, 25, 27a 2 sessions plan doc ↗ 9 items covered

Promote BillingCase into ledger pairs, the system of record, created with the invoice in one step before and independent of the Xero handoff (US-08.3.1, so a handoff fault leaves a complete pair marked "Not yet in Xero"). Each pair has a receivable leg and one payable leg, the BCTI, per receivable. A new Admin Ledger screen shows the whole ledger and each anaesthetist with an imbalance indicator and the out-of-balance list. Phase 36 now depends on 27a, not 27.

AA fee money (AA's own, never netted against payables) is never part of it; the prepay holding account's balance is subtracted (imbalance = receipts held - payables due - holding balance), and a settlement transfer moves neither received nor disbursed. Events on a Procedure and the additional invoice

Money After phases 36, 38a 2 sessions plan doc ↗ 6 items covered

Build "event" as the one thin element on a Procedure (DM-17), added at any time, with one standard Admin review step. An event raised before the Procedure's invoice is approved rides on it; one raised after is invoiced in the next run. Its first kind is the free-form additional invoice (DM-18, US-08.6.1, US-08.6.3), which replaces the post-op addendum Booking (RV-23). The office raises it on any invoiced Procedure ('Create additional invoice'). The anaesthetist raises it on their own Procedure ('Raise additional invoice'), reached through 38a's search, not an archive. It has its own number, ledger pair, Xero pair, payable and BCTI, and is linked both ways to the unchanged original. Every Procedure lists its events on mobile, web and Admin (US-03.7.3). Billing events, which absorb the former other billing lines and can be added before invoicing, plus pre-op and post-op events, come in 39b.

39

Credit notes, credit-and-rebill and the combined split

Money After phase 38b 2 sessions plan doc ↗ 8 items covered

Phase 39 (light) adds the credit tools beside 38b's additional invoice. The office can raise a credit note in full to any party, and the anaesthetist can do the same on their own Procedure, found through 38a's search. Credit in full and rebill starts from a copy of the original's lines. A split after the combined invoice is sent is a credit followed by one additional invoice per component, and the components must add up to the credit. A combination is now a line on its holder's Contract (19a), so the split has no parent procedures and no Phase 23 dependency. A split before sending is a normal admin edit: nothing is built, and there is no before-sending credit and rebill, no constant and no chip. Every credit reverses the ledger, the payable (by a negative invoice, with the paid-out part left for 39a to net) and Xero together. US-13.5.2's carve-out is built: payments, receipts and disbursements are hidden from the audit viewer, while credit notes are audited.

39a

Payment runs: the weekly cycle, BCTI approval, netting and remittance

Money After phases 37, 39 2 sessions plan doc ↗ 4 items covered

Payments to anaesthetists run on a weekly ISO-week cycle (US-10.2.7, Proposed, built to OQ-47). The office closes the week on Friday (ledger snapshot, bank reconciliation) and checks it on Monday (anomalies held out and rolled into next week). It approves the week's BCTIs (US-10.2.6) and sends the schedule on Tuesday. The accountant pays that schedule in Xero, and the engine records each payment. Each anaesthetist's negative invoices are netted against their positive payables (US-10.2.5), and each run produces a remittance advice in Admin and web Accounts (DM-25). Every payment shows its week. 27a's holding-account payables stay out of every run until its second pair releases them. Where payment is made (OQ-111, D53) is built as US-09.2.4 reads, with the detection in one place.

DM-25US-10.2.5boardUS-10.2.6boardUS-10.2.7board

Open questions: OQ-47 · OQ-111

Demo triggers and risks
  • Admin Billing monitor, payment runs: 'Close week (Friday)', 'Hold out of this run' and 'Send payment schedule (Tuesday)' (product, demo clock)
  • Admin Billing monitor: 'Approve period's BCTIs' (product)
  • Phase 39's 'Stage refund after payout', then the week's remittance shows the netted negative

Risks. The doc's 'Phase 41's trust hold' hook is now 27a's holding account: re-point it. Keep cycle days and week identity as settings. Netting is pure maths with worked examples. 37's detection must agree with the run's record. Re-baseline S4 Beat 5 figures. Catalogue screenshots: US-10.2.7, US-10.2.6 and US-10.2.5.

What to check when it's done
  • A paid prepayment held in 27a's holding account is in no run: the waiting table, the schedule and the Xero payment never take it. After the List is authorised, the second pair's payable to the anaesthetist is an ordinary line in the next run.
  • Only unheld lines of an approved, scheduled run can be paid on every payout path, including the one-click demo payouts and the PWA stand-in. Approval refuses while a Monday anomaly is open.
  • 19 positives and 1 negative are paid as one net amount, the ledger stays in balance, and the remittance advice shows the week and the netted negative in Admin and web Remittances. A held line rolls into the next week tagged Rolled from Week 30.
  • Every payment shows its week. Dr Souter's position, the GST schedule and S3 figures are unchanged after the seed is grouped into backdrop runs (Week 29 holds only pa01's payout). No FT-10.2 work remains, and the OQ-111 default is on the owner's review list.

While working:

Store, seed and pure-domain steps do not need it. Here it applies to the Billing monitor's payment cycle panel (the step rail, the waiting table, the Monday anomalies with Hold out and Mark fixed, the runs list), the run detail and its payment schedule, the remittance advice document, the Ledger's Payment runs card and caption, the week labels on payments, and the web Remittances tab, sheet and still-to-net panel.
- Mock backend only, through store actions and the audited mutate(). The ledger (Phase 36) stays the system of record and the engine never performs a disbursement: the week's schedule is paid in Xero (the accountant, simulated), and the engine records each bill payment (37's recordDisbursement) and each credit allocation (the new recordOffset) only when Xero reports it, by webhook, poll or the outage queue, idempotent by key.
- The weekly cycle is US-10.2.7: one run per ISO week, named "Week 30"; the office closes the week (the snapshot of released, unpaid payables, the ledger at close, and the reconciliation against the simulated bank download), works the Monday anomalies (hold out of this run, rolling the line into the next week tagged "Rolled from Week 30", or mark fixed), approves the week's BCTIs, and sends the payment schedule to the accountant. A payable released after the close belongs to the next week. Every payment shows the week of the run it was paid in. The demo clock does not gate the steps (it is fixed on Tue 21 Jul, ISO week 30, and forward-only): each step works in order on any day, shows its planned date from the setting and stamps the clock's actual time; the cycle never advances the clock. Log that as a built default for the owner.
- The approval gate is the point of US-10.2.6: no path pays a payable that is not an unheld line of an approved, scheduled run (runPayables, disbursePayable, the Xero-side bill payment, the Xero pair trigger, a replay, the poll, the queue). Approval refuses while a Monday anomaly is open. The one-click demo payouts approve first so the gate has no back door: the Xero sim's "Simulate payment and payout" (S3 Beat 3) and the payout half of 39's "Stage refund after payout" go through approveAndPayPairForDemo (a one-pair staged run beside the week's run, never doubling with it), and 36's PWA "Office runs payables" becomes "Office runs this week's payment cycle" (no "payables" in the label: 14's demoTriggers.test.ts rule, as 36 narrowed it to bar entries with a companion assertion that the only "payables" label is this PWA stand-in; update that companion assertion to the label set as shipped, and keep the bar rule passing as 37 left it with its "Pay anaesthetist in Xero (payables run)" entry). A run is frozen at approval; a stale run is superseded by a Re-close, never edited.
- Netting is pure billing maths in src/domain/billing/payablesRun.ts, and the week, the cycle's days, the reconciliation and the anomalies in src/domain/billing/paymentCycle.ts, both with Vitest worked examples, including US-10.2.5's 19 positives and one negative and its remittance advice criterion, US-10.2.7's held line rolling into the next week, and ISO weeks at year ends (2026 has 53). Netting uses each negative invoice's recoveryDue (what 39 left open), never its offsetAmount, and only unheld lines. Net per anaesthetist is never below zero; what a run cannot net stays open on the negative invoice and nets in a later week with positives. An anaesthetist with only negatives is not in a run. The offset is its own amount on the payable leg (offsetAmount), never counted as cash, and the whole ledger stays in balance after the close, approval, sending and detection.
- OQ-71 (answered): a negative with no later payment is handled outside the system. The only surface is the open amount on the anaesthetist's ledger position with one caption ("If no later payment comes, AA settles it with the anaesthetist outside the system") and the web still-to-net panel. No carry-forward, recovery or write-off wording or record; "Rolled from" and "Rolls into" are only for held lines.
- runExclusionFor is the only standing exclusion point. Its first reason is 'heldInHoldingAccount', from 27a's isHeldPayable (a prepaid Booking's collect payable to the holding account never enters a run; the second pair's payable to the anaesthetist is an ordinary line once released). 26's bank details are display-only, so a missing account is a Monday anomaly the office holds out or marks fixed, never an automatic exclusion; if 37 shipped a heldForBank refusal, it becomes a further reason. Phase 41 adds nothing here. A Monday hold is a per-week decision on the run's line, not an exclusion. Netting reads every open negative whatever its credit note's cause and whoever raised it.
- The 20th-of-the-month payment is not part of this cycle (Greg: the separate monthly non-trust cycle, Phase 16's AA fee run); build nothing for it and put it on the owner's review list.
- Time from the demo clock only, date-fns over given dates for ISO weeks; no Date.now(), new Date() or Math.random(). The staging bodies are deterministic.
- Seeded disbursements become backdrop weekly runs (one per ISO week, closed, approved and scheduled before paid) and every seeded receipt gets its bank line, with no figure moving: assert Dr Souter's position, the whole ledger, the GST schedule and S3's figures are identical before and after. The payout nearest today (Dr Souter's, 15 Jul; 27a holds the seeded prepayment, so it has none on 16 Jul) falls in Week 29, so the monitor opens on Week 30 with no run yet. Bump PERSIST_VERSION once for the new slices, setting, bank lines, leg field and backdrop runs, and extend the migrate and seed tests.
- Demo triggers go through the Phase 14 registry, shown only on their screen, with disabled states and bodies in src/store or src/shared: new "Stage a payment week" on the Billing monitor (choices "19 BCTIs" and "19 BCTIs and a credit after payout", service dates before the canvas horizon start, payments through the ordinary webhook with their bank lines, the credit built by one pure credit-after-payout fixture builder over 39's pure credit functions) and "Stage a bank mismatch" (session 2); re-point Phase 39's "Stage refund after payout" (payout through a staged run, result text), Phase 37's "Pay anaesthetist in Xero (payables run)" and Phase 36's PWA stand-in. Close the week, Hold out of this run, Mark fixed, Return to run, Approve week N's BCTIs, Send payment schedule, Re-close and Run payables in Xero are product buttons, not registry entries. Nothing is added to the Control Panel page. No new PWA entry is needed (the cycle, schedule and remittance advice are in Admin and web Accounts; mobile Balances is unchanged, a built default for the owner's review list); confirm the re-pointed stand-in works in the PWA build and pwaPurity.test.ts stays green.

- Follow the design files: teal is the only action colour, crimson stays identity only, pills use semantic tokens, amounts, weeks and dates are mono with tabular-nums, negatives render "-$X.XX" through formatSignedCurrency (neutral, never red), weekday names come from the setting through one helper. No en or em dashes in any app copy.

Phase goal: payments to anaesthetists run on a weekly cycle named by its ISO week, which the office closes (snapshot and bank reconciliation), checks (anomalies held out and rolled into the next week), approves (the week's BCTIs, before anything is paid) and schedules for the accountant, who pays it in Xero; each anaesthetist's negative invoices are netted against their positive payables, paid as one net amount and shown on a remittance advice in Admin and web Accounts; every payment shows the week it was paid in; and a negative with no later payment to net against is left to AA to settle outside the system, visible on the anaesthetist's ledger position.

The office's Waiting for NHI view (/admin/patients/waiting) is derived from 33's waitingForNhi rows: the patient as received, the List or date, the surgeon's rooms (HPI CPN then name, else the hospital's email), an Urgent pill when the date is within WAITING_NHI_URGENT_WITHIN_DAYS (3), Email rooms (a real mailto link from Phase 35's builder, allowlisted: no DOB, no NHI, no money, no notes) and Add NHI. Add NHI (addNhiToWaitingRow) validates the NHI, calls 33's correctImportRow and releases the row; it applies nothing, and the office's decision on the matching screen makes the Booking and the one patient record.

- The patient balance is a rule in 15a's warning routine (OQ-41 and OQ-74 answered, D24), not a separate alert store. It checks a Booking only when its payer on the Booking is the patient (checksPatientBalance over 21's Booking.payer, the one gate; the Contract does not gate it, and a payer changed to a guardian through setBookingPayer removes it at the next evaluation), and it counts only invoices billed to the patient themself (hospital, insurer, other holder, named-payer 'payer', AA fee and credited invoices never count as owing; the Booking's own invoices, its prepayment invoice included, are excluded). Owing within the threshold is a mild (yellow) warning (the 30-day case is mild, not silent); strictly older than the threshold is strong (red); a credit held for the patient with nothing owing is mild; the age counts from the invoice date in one function (invoiceAgeDays). It is before-procedure (our reading, logged), office-audience only (add an audience field to 15a's WarningRule, default all, so every other rule still shows in both apps), and never blocks: staff go ahead and Clear it from the to-do list. NHI lookup and identity standards

Patients After phases 26, 40 1 session plan doc ↗ 2 items covered

Bring NZ identity standards up to the catalogue on the current add-booking forms (mobile, web, admin phone advice). The NHI is validated as typed, and only a valid NHI is looked up through a simulated Digital Services Hub over a deterministic synthetic register. The Hub has checking, slow and unavailable states with a manual fallback and Retry, and a purpose statement. The NHI is required (D11), so Save needs a valid one even when the Hub is down. The RVG code is a type-ahead and typed procedure text is source text; the lookup touches neither, and the payer follows the found patient unless it was already changed to a guardian. The office can refresh a patient from the register, stamped "Last refreshed". HPI CPN is the one practitioner label and format.

Scale and privacy

NFR After phases 34, 36, 37, 42 2 sessions plan doc ↗ 2 items covered

A presenter can load the whole practice in memory (85 anaesthetists, about 20,000 sessions over the scheduling horizon, about 28,000 invoices a year) and watch Admin Day, Invoices, Audit and the processing monitor page, sort and filter at that scale with measured timings. The generated set follows the 2026-10-20 model: RVG groups with no procedure list, holders with settings, Contracts with or without lines, a payer and a valid NHI on every Booking, values held on the Procedure, and a small prepaid handful with holding-account pairs. The presenter can also show the privacy policy working: a restricted, audited, masked raw hospital row, an NHI and personal-information leak scan (nothing outside the core platform, nothing in Xero), and a Synthetic data only badge in every app.

US-15.0.4boardUS-15.0.6board
Demo triggers and risks
  • Admin Day and Invoices: 'Load full-scale data'
  • Data Inspector: 'Scan for NHI leaks'
  • Matching screen, selected unmatched row: 'View raw row'

Risks. The doc's generator spec (procedures, general procedures, price precedence and price source, prepaid sets, first-party Contracts, provisional NHI, archive) is superseded: rewrite it to the shapes above. localStorage cannot hold the data: pause persistence with a banner. Session 1 the generator with integrity tests (a payer, an NHI, one primary and one fitting Contract per Procedure); session 2 the scaled screens and privacy. Deterministic.

What to check when it's done
  • Load full-scale data (with its confirm) shows the banner with 85 anaesthetists, 20,000+ sessions over the horizon setting, 27,500 to 28,500 invoices and a generation time, with saving paused. Reset or a reload returns the pristine seed.
  • A generated Booking has a patient with a valid NHI and a payer. Each Procedure shows its description as received, an optional RVG code and exactly one Contract (No contract (RVG) or a holder-fit Contract). The age modifier and P1 are pre-applied and removable. A prepaid Booking is priced at its line's price, and the prepay holding account balances.
  • Admin Day (30 per page), Invoices (50, with search), Audit (100) and the Billing monitor (20 anaesthetist groups, Problems only applied before paging) page at scale with demo-scale and full-scale timings in the banner's Timings table. At demo scale none of them shows a pager.
  • Matching raw row: View raw row asks for a reason, shows a masked payload and is audited. 'View raw row as another role' is refused and audited. Scan for NHI leaks reports 0 found per area (the Xero row checks personal details too), the planted leak gives exactly one masked hit, and the Synthetic data only badge shows in every app.

- The generator builds the 2026-10-20 model through the one billing module in aa-prototype/src/domain/billing (plus the seed's builders), the same structures, candidate rule, resolver, held-value calculation, who-is-billed function, snapshot builder and prepayment builders the app uses, never a second copy of the shapes, so a change to the technical design (AR-29, AR-30) stays a contained edit there; a source-scan test proves fullScale/ takes that logic only from domain/billing. If a rule it needs is missing or wrong, fix it in that module with its test and log it. Standing patterns are recurring bookings (Phase 30), never Permanent List templates. Assigned Lists are ACTIVE, Draft Lists DRAFT. RVG groups have no procedure list: a Procedure keeps its description as received (from the pool 20a seeded from AR-35) and an optional RVG code from the group master. Every Booking has a patient with a valid NHI and a payer (Phase 21), prefilled from the patient or a guardian for a child. Each Procedure has exactly one Contract chosen by Phase 20's rule: No contract (RVG) or a Contract whose holder fits the Booking, with a version in force on the List date and a line for the Procedure (or a Contract with no lines); never a hospital, insurer or procedure default, because none exists. Its price, rate and discount are held on the Procedure from the starting values (line or group) and priced by Phase 24's calculation; its modifiers are records (age and P1 pre-applied and removable, the odd optional one with its explanation; no ASA pre-fill). Who is billed comes from Phase 21's one function. A practice-sized handful (prepaidShare) of Bookings sit on office-kept price-list Contracts flagged prepaid, with a person as payer, priced at the line's price, the prepayment pair to the prepay holding account and, once AUTHORISED, the second pair to the anaesthetist (Phases 27 and 27a); log the share. Nothing generated carries a removed field (payment category, route, funderOverride, a Contract kind, an estimate or deposit).
- Generated history goes through the same pure builders the billing run and the ledger use (the pricing snapshot written at authorise, invoices priced only from it, one BCTI per receivable invoice, ledger pairs, the holding account's pairs, disbursements on Phase 39a's weekly cycle, Xero mirror with Phase 16's no-personal-information contact labels), never through store actions, and every ledger pair balances. The integrity tests check every Booking has a payer and a valid NHI and exactly one primary Procedure, every Procedure exactly one Contract that fits Phase 20's rule, its description as received and its pre-applied modifiers, every AUTHORISED Procedure a snapshot whose price Phase 24's calculation reproduces (AR-29 integrity-rules), every prepaid Booking on a prepaid Contract with a person as payer, and the holding account in balance with nothing paid out before AUTHORISED; the AA-FEE invoices are monthly per anaesthetist with the per-BCTI charge from Phase 16's one count function (D1); the audit trail uses only the runtime's own codes (no invented payment or disbursement entries, per US-13.5.2); billed history raises no open warnings; a small deterministic share of authorised Lists carry a problem the Billing monitor recognises. Ids come from the counters, generated invoice numbers use a reserved series, and the next runtime id is unused.

Reset resumes saving before it installs the pristine seed; a reload after loading returns the pristine seed; the pause is separate from the storage-error latch. The scale mode and timings live in a non-persisted store.

Milestones

What a workshop can be shown once each milestone phase is done.

  • After phase 16
    Built. Booking vocabulary everywhere, with Copy a Booking gone, photo capture out of the Add a booking chooser and an assigned List called ACTIVE. Every demo action on its own screen, in the harness bar and on a handset. Warnings, never blocks: one routine, the to-do list, a triangle on Bookings, the prepayment gate turned into a warning, no confirm step at submit. The payable equals the receivable, AA's fee is a monthly invoice, and Xero holds no patient names.
  • After phase 38a
    The office's schedule (28 to 32 built, finished by 32a and 32b): every session stored and free by default over a configurable horizon, Slots and Lists, statuses as a user-maintained list, the availability calendar, recurring bookings, Draft Lists assigned by the office with preferences and tiers and never onto an unavailable session; unavailability, sickness included, forcing a return or hand-on and never a conflict, the conflict dashboard showing hospital closures; whoever moves a List choosing what the vacated session becomes; Lists handed on and single Bookings moved into a free colleague's session as a new List; the notification pool with notices ticked resolved and alerts from a List or Booking; and the anaesthetist changing a submitted List until it is authorised, a main view from today and a search for past work. S2 is re-scripted.
  • After phase 25
    The catalogue's pricing model end to end: contract holders with an 'is billed' setting and Contracts with settings (editable, prepaid), dated versions never backdated, AA codes and one No contract (RVG) held by AA; RVG groups as the one master list and an optional RVG code by type-ahead; standalone lines, Contracts with no lines, combinations as lines and the anaesthetists' price lists, with starting values from the line or the RVG group and any base value accepted with an office warning; optional itemised modifiers with explanations, age and P1 pre-applied and removable; one Contract per Procedure, mandatory at setup, picked from Contracts then lines, changeable by the anaesthetist until AUTHORISED; the rooms', hospital's and invoice descriptions with the Contract and RVG code on every booking screen; the payer on the Booking, who is billed by the Contract, the insurer and approval number, warnings, and completion needing a Contract; invoices sent by the run with the invoice description and a Split button; the RVG multi-procedure rule; prices on the Procedure with a discount line, a $0 invoice and the editable flag, the office changing any price with no reason; staged Contract changes submitted as new versions that relink un-invoiced work, and a lock at AUTHORISED that reproduces invoices. S1 Beat 3, S2 Beat 2, S3, S4 Beat 3 and S5 are re-scripted.
  • After phase 27a
    Prepayment started by picking a Contract flagged prepaid for a person paying: the amount is that line's price, in full and shown to the anaesthetist; the invoice generated when an admin approves it, its payable held in the prepay holding account; part-paid tracking and a warning that strengthens as the date nears; at authorisation the prepaid Procedure priced at its amount with nothing raised automatically, and a second pair paying whoever did the List. S4 Beat 1 is re-scripted.
  • After phase 35
    S1 rebuilt: one theatre list a day from the two integrated hospitals onto the review-and-merge screen showing each row's wording as received, rows without an NHI waiting, a day move as a cancellation plus a new Booking, then a Booking whose Contract the office sets (No contract (RVG) first). Explicit save with change sets, and the on-demand update email from the change history, from a template, to the rooms or the hospital, including from a List-move notice.
  • After phase 39a
    The money story on the internal ledger: balances in or out of balance, the holding account's legs and second pairs, Xero mirror resilience and a processing monitor grouped by anaesthetist, ledger-backed web accounts with a flat outstanding list and a monthly GST report of payments passed, events with additional invoices for office and anaesthetist, the credit note option, credit-and-rebill from copied lines and a combination split after sending that equals the credit, and weekly ISO-week payment runs with BCTI approval, netting and a remittance advice. S4 Beats 2 to 5 are re-scripted.
  • After phase 44
    Every verified gap closed: pre-op, post-op and billing events on every Procedure (no billing lines), patients with a mandatory NHI, intake rows waiting for one, balance warnings, follow-up tools and NHI lookup, prepayment letters, by-hand settlement with part credits, refunds from the holding account, a moved prepaid Booking changing nothing, reference-data loads, full-scale and privacy demos, anaesthetist sign-in, point-of-need help, and the rewritten S1 to S5 run sheet.
